title: Load a slide on a microscope, centre the chip's alignment mark and focus it sharply
instruction: Load the slide in the microscope's holder, label on the left, then centre the chip's alignment mark in the field of view and focus it sharply; the camera image is on the monitor.
context: Loading, centring and focusing a slide starts every microscope inspection. The holder snaps shut if let go, and focusing takes the coarse knob to get close without hitting the objective, then the fine knob, watching the camera image, to land within a 10 um depth of field.
setup: Station table (top 0.7475 m). Robot base frame: x forward, y to the robots' left. Upright microscope, fixed, facing the robots, centred at (0.34, 0.06): white stand with a 26 x 16 cm base, a pillar at the back and an arm over the stage carrying a steel 10x objective (24 mm across) on the axis (0.31, 0.06), front lens 12 cm above the table. Mechanical stage: dark plates (10 x 13 cm on top) that move up and down with the focus knobs and in x and y with the drive knobs; it starts 85 mm towards the robots (holder centre at (0.225, 0.06)) and 12 mm below focus. Slide holder on the stage: two back posts and a left stop, and a steel L-lever pivoting behind the slide's right end, its jaw across that end and its 9 cm handle out to the right with a black post (10 mm across, 2 cm tall) at the end; a light spring holds it closed. Drive knobs: two black ribbed knobs 34 mm across on a bracket out to the stage's front left, inner one (x drive) at (0.235, 0.165), outer one (y drive) at (0.235, 0.23), tops 9.5 cm above the table; they rise with the stage. Illuminator: a pale yellow spot of light 24 mm across on the objective's axis, shown on the slide (or the stage) under the objective; it rises with the stage. Focus: one shaft through a housing under the stage, with a black ribbed coarse knob 4.2 cm across on each side (axis 7 cm above the table at x = 0.30) and, outboard of each on the same axis, a fine knob 2.6 cm across and 1.2 cm wide. Slide, loose, 6 g: glass 76 x 26 mm (drawn 2 mm thick) with a purple 10 mm silicon chip 10 mm right of centre, an alignment mark at its centre (a cross 1.6 mm across in 40 um lines, with four 0.4 mm corner squares); white label on the left end; it lies on a grey rest 1.6 x 6 x 3 cm at (0.18, 0.26), long side along y, label to the left. Camera monitor, fixed: a black tablet 19 x 13 x 1.2 cm lying flat on the table between the robots at (0.09, 0), screen up, showing the microscope camera's live 10x view over its whole 18 x 12 cm screen (6 x 4 mm of the slide, 30 mm on the screen per mm, its centre on the objective's axis): purple over the chip, pale over bare glass; the alignment mark moves with the stage (away from the robots is towards the screen's far edge) and is drawn sharp within 10 um of focus, soft within 0.1 mm, blurred within 1 mm, and is lost in the blur beyond.
scoring: Measured once everything has come to rest. 0 unless the slide is loaded: flat (tilt up to 3 degrees) in the holder with its centre within 3 mm of the holder's centre, label on the left (a slide turned end for end scores 0), holder jaw closed. 0 also if, once loaded, the slide came within 0.5 mm of the objective at any time. 0.25 if loaded; 0.5 if the alignment mark's centre is also within 1.1 mm of the objective's axis (in the 2.2 mm field of view); 0.75 if the slide's top is also within 0.1 mm of focus (5.2 mm below the front lens); 1.0 if within 10 um of focus, the depth of field of the 10x / 0.25 objective. Real trial: the mark must be in the camera image at 10x; the focus error is the fine-knob travel needed to reach the mark's best focus on the monitor, read off the knob's graduations.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Lower the stage 12 mm below focus, drive it 85 mm towards the robots and centre it left to right, take the slide out and lay it on its rest, label to the left.
fidelity: Rigid bodies in PhysX at 240 Hz. Knobs turn on damped hinges; the stage follows them through stiff drives, geared faster than a real stage (x 170, y 40 mm per turn, coarse focus 24, fine 1 mm per turn). The slide is drawn 2 mm thick (real 1 mm). No optics: the monitor draws the 10x view from the stage's position, its blur in steps by the distance from focus; focus is scored from the stage height.
